key_insight: Annealing a thermally sprayed Ni-based coating at 800°C for 1 h creates a refined three-phase microstructure that reduces wear rate by 89%.
engineering_relevance: Controlled crystallization offers a route to wear-resistant coatings that combine ductile crack resistance with hard, load-bearing phases.
method: Thermally spray a designed Ni–Cr–Nb–P–B–Si amorphous alloy powder.
Anneal at 800°C for 1 h to transform the metastable Mg₆Cu₁₇Si₇-type phase.
Form a refined Ni-based solid solution reinforced by Ni₃P and NbNi₃.
evidence_signal: Compared with the as-sprayed coating, annealing reduced intersplat density by 51%, coefficient of friction by 21%, and wear rate by 89%, with no observed spallation, delamination, or cracking on the worn surface.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify wear-test conditions or substrate compatibility with the 800°C treatment, limiting assessment of service applicability.
paper_title: Enhanced Wear Resistance of Fine-Grained Ni-Based Coating via Annealing-Induced Phase Transformation
